name: SECOND
description: SECOND extracts the second (0-59) from a time or date-time serial number, reading only the fractional time portion of the value.
tldr: Returns the second portion (0-59) of a time value.

parameters.name: serial_number
parameters.description: A date-time serial (or a time fraction). The integer part is a date and the fractional part is the time; the second is taken from the fractional part.

basicExample.description: Get the second from a time
basicExample.explanation: TIME(12,30,45) is 12:30:45 PM, so SECOND returns 45.

advancedExamples.title: Extract second from a date-time serial
advancedExamples.description: SECOND reads the fractional time part
advancedExamples.explanation: The .520833 fraction equals 12:30:00 exactly, so SECOND returns 0.

advancedExamples.title: Seconds from a precise time
advancedExamples.explanation: 9:15:30 AM has 30 seconds, so SECOND returns 30.

howItWorks: SECOND takes the fractional part of the serial (the time-of-day component), multiplies it by 86400 (seconds in a day), and returns the remainder after removing whole minutes, giving an integer from 0 to 59. The date portion is ignored.

howToSteps.name: Reference a time value
howToSteps.text: Point SECOND at a cell or expression that holds a time or date-time.

limitations: SECOND ignores the date portion entirely.
A value with no time fraction (a whole number) returns 0.
It accepts only valid serials; text times must be converted first.

commonErrors.cause: The argument is text that Excel cannot parse as a time.
commonErrors.fix: Convert the text to a real time serial first (e.g. with TIMEVALUE).

commonErrors.cause: The serial is a whole number with no time part, or the time has zero seconds.
commonErrors.fix: Make sure the value actually contains a non-zero second.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: SECOND works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Does SECOND work on a full date-time?
faq.answer: Yes, it reads only the time fraction, e.g. 2024-01-15 12:30:45 returns 45.

faq.question: What is the maximum second returned?
faq.answer: The maximum is 59, because times are stored as fractions under 1.

faq.question: Why do I get 0 for a whole-minute time?
faq.answer: Whole-minute times have a zero seconds component.
